name: Finnish Romani
catalog_citation: Granqvist, Kimmo. 2002. Finnish Romani phonology and dialect geography. SKY Journal of Linguistics 15: 61-83.
catalog_locator: Section 7 "Stress", p. 77 (PDF p. 17 of the copy we hold; running head FINNISH ROMANI PHONOLOGY 77); also p. 75 (PDF p. 15), section on syllable structure
catalog_quote: Unlike in many other Romani dialects, in Finnish and Hungarian Romani, the primary stress is placed on the initial syllable, e.g. ['kɑːlo] 'black', ['tʃɑːʋe] 'boys' (Valtonen 1968: 58; Hedman 1996). The stress system, thus, coincides with the Finnish system as for the primary stress. As for the secondary stress, this must be still empirically checked. ... Valtonen (1968: 132) reports that one of his informants used forms like ['teŋkɑʋeːhɑ] 'think+TR+PRES. SG2' arising from [teŋkɑ'ʋesɑ] instead of today's ['teŋkɑʋehɑ].
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Unlike in many other Romani dialects, in Finnish and Hungarian Romani, the primary stress is placed on the initial syllable, e.g. ['kɑ:lo] 'black', ['tʃɑ:ʋe] 'boys' (Valtonen 1968: 58; Hedman 1996). The stress system, thus, coincides with the Finnish system as for the primary stress. As for the secondary stress, this must be still empirically checked.
new_statements.citation: Granqvist, Kimmo. 2002. Finnish Romani phonology and dialect geography. SKY Journal of Linguistics 15: 61-83.
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (23 pp., journal pp. 61-83, not encrypted). Section "7. Stress" is on PDF page 17 = journal p. 77 (running head "FINNISH ROMANI PHONOLOGY 77"); I rendered the page image (150 dpi) and read it directly because the text layer garbles the IPA. The passage is there verbatim: "Unlike in many other Romani dialects, in Finnish and Hungarian Romani, the primary stress is placed on the initial syllable, e.g. ['kɑ:lo] 'black', ['tʃɑ:ʋe] 'boys' (Valtonen 1968: 58; Hedman 1996). The stress system, thus, coincides with the Finnish system as for the primary stress. As for the secondary stress, this must be still empirically checked." The following paragraph on the same page links the stress shift…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the first syllable of every word, as in Finnish; this is a historical shift from the Common Romani final/stem-final pattern, which the author links to the preference for heavy (bimoraic) initial syllables.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Granqvist 2002: 77 says secondary stress 'must be still empirically checked'. Granqvist 2024 (Suomen romanikielen varhaiset vuodet, p. 161) reads Thesleff's 1901 paradigms as showing Finnish-type secondary stress (phúrjuv-àah-a). Thesleff 1901: VII notes a Nebenaccent on the -i- of -iba nouns (boliba).
new_statements.exceptions: None in Granqvist 2002. Thesleff 1901: VII (1890s data): accent varies by region, is mostly initial, but falls on the second syllable in words with the negative prefix bi- and the Swedish prefix för- (bičačo, förbarmava).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (lexical words, citation forms cited in IPA); the paper's corpus is 140,000 words of Finnish Romani collected 2000-2001. Same statement repeated by Granqvist 2012 (Romano džaniben 19(1): 31, in Czech: 'Hlavní přízvuk je na první slabice jako ve finštině') and independently by Vuorela & Borin 1998: 69 ('The accent is normally fixed on the first syllable of word forms, on the Finnish pattern').
new_statements.identity_note: Sources describe Finnish Romani / Finnish Kalo as a whole (glottocode kalo1256). Thesleff 1901 notes regional variation in accent placement in the 1890s data; Granqvist 2002 distinguishes Eastern and Western/Northern subdialects for segmental features but gives one stress rule for the language.

sources.note: Section 7 Stress, p. 77: primary stress always on the initial syllable (as in Finnish and Hungarian Romani), citing Valtonen 1968: 58 and Hedman 1996; secondary stress not yet checked empirically; p. 75 also states 'primary stress always on the initial syllable'; p. 78 calls the shift from word-final to first-syllable stress one of the most significant historical changes.

sources.note: Vorwort p. VII (PDF p. 12, verified on the page image): 'Der Accent in der finnländischen Zigeunermundart variiert nach den verschiedenen Gegenden des Landes. Meistens ist er jedoch auf der ersten Silbe; wo dies nicht der Fall ist, ist er bezeichnet, ausser in den Wörtern, welche mit der Negation bi- oder mit der schwedischen Vorsilbe för- anfangen, in welchen Fällen der Accent auf der zweiten Silbe liegt (z. B. bičačo, förbarmava). Die Wörter auf -iba haben einen Nebenaccent auf i.'
